builder_plan.scenario: Long customer conversations exhaust memory or limit concurrent requests.
builder_plan.change: Change only the attention cache policy, after checking model and runtime support.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model with its ordinary attention cache.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak cache memory, long-context answer quality, first-token latency, and requests completed.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Lachesis: Lifetime-Aware KV Cache Placement for Agent Serving across HBM and High-Bandwidth Flash
summary: The method replaces lifetime-agnostic (HBM-first) KV cache placement with a layer between the agent harness and the serving engine that writes each KV segment to HBM or high-bandwidth flash based on its predicted lifetime, inferred from temporal, structural, and inter-worker behavior of the harness. The cost is an additional placement and eviction layer, dependence on high-bandwidth flash hardware that is not yet generally available, and harness analysis to characterize segment lifetimes. It can fail if lifetime predictions misclassify long-lived segments into flash, accelerating wear beyond endurance limits, and its results are trace-driven simulation rather than measurements on a deployed system.
rationale: The technique targets high-bandwidth flash hardware and multi-agent serving at continuous full load, neither of which is available to a reader on a single 24 GB GPU or API budget, so it is worth tracking but not actionable now.
technique: Lifetime-aware KV cache placement across HBM and flash

claims.statement: The method replaces lifetime-agnostic (HBM-first) KV cache placement with a layer between the agent harness and the serving engine that writes each KV segment to HBM or high-bandwidth flash based on its predicted lifetime, inferred from temporal, structural, and inter-worker behavior of the harness. The cost is an additional placement and eviction layer, dependence on high-bandwidth flash hardware that is not yet generally available, and harness analysis to characterize segment lifetimes. It can fail if lifetime predictions misclassify long-lived segments into flash, accelerating wear beyond endurance limits, and its results are trace-driven simulation rather than measurements on a deployed system.

In trace-driven simulation, extends HBF device lifetime by 1.19-3.13x over HBM-first placement, reaching 3.3-12.2 device-years and exceeding the five-year warranty on the multi-agent trace under continuous full load.
